invalidating_assumptions: TESTED & FALSIFIED: the v1 contract assumed #B1 (runtime pkg) / #B3 (SDK) were hard blockers for ANY showcase. showcase.py is built directly on the existing `fak preflight` seam and its captured run discharges A1-A5 without #B1/#B3 — so the dependency gating was too strict for the governance core. If a maintainer nonetheless rules the showcase MUST sit on the #B1 runtime + #B3 SDK to count, this dogfood is a stepping stone, not the deliverable.

Assumes 'a captured live run as its proof' is satisfied model-free for GOVERNANCE. If the acceptance means the PROPOSALS must also come from a live model (not a scripted trajectory), then a live-model capture is still required and this witness is partial on that axis (kernel verdicts real; proposals scripted).

Assumes a cost CAP means an enforced ceiling that halts spend. showcase.py demonstrates exactly that mechanism; if 'cost cap' instead means only a real token-denominated bill, A4 needs the #B1 runtime seam to bind the cap to live tokens.
